ja: だいななじゅうにかい

p.src: Yuanyang, meanwhile, went out through the side gate, her face still flushed and her heart pounding at this truly unexpected occurrence. She reflected that this was no ordinary matter: if she spoke of it, illicit love and trespass would become entangled, lives might be at stake, and others could well be implicated. Since it had nothing to do with her anyway, she resolved to keep it to herself and tell no one. She returned to her room, reported back to Grandmother Jia, and everyone retired for the night. From then on, she seldom entered the Garden after dark. If such a strange thing could happen in the Garden, she thought, what might not happen elsewhere? Consequently, she became reluctant to go about in other places as well.

p.src: As it happened, Siqi had grown up playing and living together with her maternal aunt's son. In childish jest, they had pledged that in the future neither would marry anyone else. In recent years they had grown up, each becoming handsome and charming. Whenever Siqi went home, they exchanged amorous glances and cherished their old affection, though they had never found an opportunity to consummate it. Both feared that their parents would refuse consent, so between them they arranged to bribe the old women in the Garden to leave a gate open and keep watch. Only today, taking advantage of the confusion, had they met in secret for the first time. Though they had not yet become one, they had sworn eternal love and privately exchanged tokens, enjoying boundless tenderness between them. Suddenly startled apart by Yuanyang, the young servant had already slipped through flowers and willows and escaped by the side gate. Siqi could not sleep all night and was filled with regret. When she saw Yuanyang the next day, her face turned red and then pale, and she was overcome with embarrassment. Tormented by her guilty secret, she had no appetite for food or tea and moved about in a daze. After enduring two days without hearing of any disturbance, she at last set her mind somewhat at ease. That evening, however, an old woman came and whispered to her, “Your cousin has actually run away and has not returned home for three or four days. They have now sent people to search for him everywhere.” On hearing this, Siqi nearly fell backward with rage. She thought, “Even if the scandal had broken, we ought to have died together. He considers himself a man, yet he was the first to flee. Clearly he has no true feeling.” This added a fresh grievance to her distress. The next day she felt unwell at heart and could no longer hold herself together. She took to her bed and, wasting away in misery, became seriously ill. When Yuanyang heard that a young servant over there had disappeared without cause, while Siqi in the Garden had fallen gravely ill and was to be moved outside, she felt certain that both were terrified of being punished: “They must be so frightened because they fear I will tell.” She consequently felt sorry for them. On the pretext of visiting Siqi, she sent everyone else out, then stood solemnly and swore to her: “If I tell a single person, may retribution strike me dead at once! Just set your mind at ease and recover; do not needlessly throw away your young life.” Siqi seized her hand and wept. “Dear sister, we have been intimate since childhood. You have never treated me as an outsider, and I have never dared slight you. Though I have now taken one false step, if you truly tell no one, you will be as my own mother to me. From this day on, every day I live will be a day you have given me. When I recover, I shall set up a tablet to pray for your long life and burn incense before it every day, praying that you may enjoy both happiness and longevity all your life. If I die, I shall become a donkey or a dog to repay you. Besides, as the saying goes, ‘However long the pavilion may stretch, no banquet lasts forever.’ In another two or three years, all of us will have to leave this place.

p.src: Another saying goes, ‘Even drifting duckweed meets again someday; how could people never meet again?’ If we should meet again one day, how could I ever repay your goodness then?” She wept as she spoke. Her words so touched Yuanyang's heart that she too began to weep. She nodded and said, “That is quite true. I am not one of those in charge. Why should I ruin your good name merely to curry favor for myself? Besides, this is not a matter I could readily speak of to anyone myself. You may set your mind at rest. Once you recover, however, you must behave yourself and never act recklessly again.” Siqi nodded repeatedly on her pillow. Yuanyang comforted her a while longer before leaving. Knowing that Jia Lian was away and having noticed that Xifeng had seemed listless in voice and manner these past two days, unlike her usual self, Yuanyang stopped by to see her as well. When she entered Xifeng's courtyard, the attendants at the inner gate saw who it was and rose to let her pass. Yuanyang had just reached the main room when Ping'er emerged from the inner chamber. Seeing her, Ping'er hurried over and said with a quiet smile, “She ate only a mouthful before lying down for her midday rest. Sit in this room for a little while.” Yuanyang had no choice but to accompany Ping'er into the room on the east side. A young maid brought them tea. Yuanyang asked softly, “What has been wrong with your mistress these past two days? She seems so listless to me.” Since no one else was in the room, Ping'er sighed and replied, “She has not been listless only since today; she was already like this a month ago. Then these last few days brought a great deal of bustle and annoyance, which aggravated the trouble again. In the past two days her illness has worsened, so she can no longer keep up appearances and it has begun to show.” Yuanyang hastily asked, “If so, why did you not summon a physician earlier to treat her?” Ping'er sighed. “Dear sister, surely you know her temper. Never mind summoning a physician and taking medicine. I could not bear to watch and merely asked how she was feeling, but she grew angry and accused me instead of cursing her with illness. Even in this state, she still spends every day prying here and investigating there, refusing to let things go and tend to her health.” Yuanyang said, “Even so, you really should have a physician examine her and determine the illness, so that everyone can be reassured.” Ping'er replied, “Dear sister, speaking of her illness, it does not seem a minor complaint to me.” Yuanyang quickly asked, “What illness is it?” At this question, Ping'er leaned a little closer and whispered in her ear, “Ever since her monthly courses began last month, the bleeding has continued little by little for an entire month without stopping. Would you not call that a serious illness?” On hearing this, Yuanyang exclaimed, “Oh dear!”

p.src: “By what you say, wouldn’t that amount to a veritable hemorrhage?” Pinger hastily spat in disapproval, then laughed softly. “What a thing for an unmarried girl to say! You really do know how to curse people.” At this, Yuanyang could not help blushing. She too laughed softly and said, “To tell the truth, I don’t even know what this ‘hemorrhage’ is. Have you forgotten that my elder sister died of this very illness before me? I had no idea what the illness was. I happened to overhear Mother discussing it with my sister’s mother-in-law and was puzzled; only later, when Mother explained the cause in detail, did I come to understand a little of it.” Pinger laughed. “Of course you would know. I had completely forgotten.”

p.src: While the two were talking, a young maid came in and said to Pinger, “Madam Zhu came again just now. We told her that our mistress had only just lain down for her afternoon nap, so she went over to see Madam Wang.” Pinger nodded on hearing this. Yuanyang asked, “Which Madam Zhu?” Pinger replied, “Sister-in-law Zhu, the official matchmaker. Some official named Sun has sent her to propose a marriage with our family, so for the past two days she has brought a written proposal every day and pestered us without end.” Before she had finished, the young maid came running back to announce, “Second Master is coming in.” Even as she spoke, Jia Lian had reached the main-room door and was calling for Pinger. Pinger answered and had only just gone out to meet him when Jia Lian came searching into this room. At the doorway he suddenly saw Yuanyang seated on the kang and stopped short. Smiling, he said, “Sister Yuanyang, how honored this humble place is by your noble feet today!” Yuanyang remained seated and replied with a smile, “I came to pay my respects to Master and Mistress, but as luck would have it, one is away and the other asleep.” Jia Lian laughed. “You work hard all year long attending to the Old Lady, Sister, and I have not even been to see you. How could I dare trouble you to come and see us? What perfect timing! I was just about to go and look for you. This robe was too hot, so I came here first to change into a lined one before going to find you. Heaven has taken pity on me and spared me the journey: here you are, waiting for me already.” As he spoke, he sat down in a chair. Yuanyang asked, “What do you want this time?” Jia Lian smiled before replying. “There is a certain matter I have completely forgotten, but perhaps you still remember it. For the Old Lady’s birthday last year, a monk from out of town presented her with a bergamot fashioned from congealed wax. She liked it and had it brought in at once for display. When it was her birthday the other day, I saw that item still entered in the antiques ledger, but I have no idea where it has gone now. The people in the antiques storehouse have reported it to me twice as well; once I have found out for certain, I can make the proper entry. So I wanted to ask you whether the Old Lady still has it on display or whether it was handed over to someone else.” Yuanyang replied, “The Old Lady displayed it for a few days, then tired of it and gave it to your wife. And now you come asking me about it! I even remember the day; it was I who sent old Wang’s wife to deliver it. If you have forgotten, ask your wife or Pinger.” Pinger was fetching clothes. Hearing this, she hurried out and said, “It was handed over to us and is upstairs now. Mistress already sent someone to tell them it had been given to this household. Those muddleheads failed to enter it and have come stirring up these trivial matters again.”

p.src: Jia Lian laughed when he heard this. “If it was given to your mistress, why did I know nothing of it? You must have secretly appropriated it.” Pinger replied, “Mistress told you about it, but you wanted to give it away. She refused and only with difficulty managed to keep it. Now you have forgotten it yourself and accuse us of appropriating it. What treasure is it, anyway? It is hardly something rare. We have never once appropriated anything ten times finer than that; why would we suddenly take a fancy to such a worthless thing?” Jia Lian lowered his head and pondered with a smile. Then he clapped his hands and exclaimed, “How muddleheaded I have become! I forget one thing after another and bring complaints upon myself. I am nothing like the man I used to be.” Yuanyang laughed. “You can hardly be blamed. You have so much business to attend to and so many people talking at you; add a couple of cups of wine, and how could you possibly keep everything straight?” As she spoke, she rose to leave. Jia Lian hurriedly stood as well. “Dear Sister, stay a little longer. Your younger brother still has a favor to ask.” Then he scolded the young maid. “Why haven’t you brewed some good tea? Quickly, take a clean lidded bowl and brew a cup of the new tea presented yesterday.” Then he said to Yuanyang, “These last few days, because of the Old Lady’s birthday, we have spent all the several thousand taels of silver we had. The rents and land revenues from several places will not come in until September, so at present we cannot make ends meet. Tomorrow we must send gifts to the Prince of Nan’an’s household, prepare the Double Ninth gifts for Her Highness, and meet several other substantial obligations for weddings and funerals. We shall need at least another two or three thousand taels, and it is difficult to borrow such a sum at short notice. As the proverb says, ‘Better to rely on oneself than to ask favors of others.’ There is no help for it: you must risk some blame, Sister, and secretly bring out a chest of the Old Lady’s gold and silver articles that she is unlikely to miss. We can pawn them temporarily for a thousand taels or so and tide ourselves over. Within six months, once the silver comes in, I shall redeem everything and return it. I certainly will not let you bear the blame.” Yuanyang laughed. “You certainly know how to devise new schemes! How ever did you think of this one?” Jia Lian laughed. “I am not exaggerating: apart from you, there are others who manage gold and silver worth a thousand taels or so, but none of them is as sensible or courageous as you. If I mentioned it to them, I would only frighten them out of their wits. That is why I would ‘rather strike a golden bell once than beat a broken drum three thousand times.’” Before he had finished, a young maid from Grandmother Jia’s quarters hurried in looking for Yuanyang. “The Old Lady has been looking for you for ages, Sister. We could not find you anywhere—and here you are!” On hearing this, Yuanyang hurried away at once to see Grandmother Jia. When Jia Lian saw her leave, he had no choice but to go back and see Xifeng. As it happened, Xifeng was already awake. She had overheard him asking Yuanyang to pawn the valuables but did not find it convenient to speak, so she merely lay on the couch.

p.src: When she heard that Yuanyang had gone, Jia Lian came in, and Xifeng asked him, “Has she agreed?” Jia Lian said with a smile, “She hasn’t agreed yet, but it’s partly settled. If you speak to her again this evening, it will be certain.” Xifeng laughed. “I’m having nothing to do with this. Suppose she agrees: you may make fine promises now, but once you have the money, you’ll put the whole matter out of your mind. Who will be left to haggle with you then? And if the Old Lady finds out, all the respectability I’ve built up over these past years will be lost.” “My dear,” Jia Lian said with a smile, “if you settle it for me, how shall I reward you?” Xifeng laughed. “Tell me, what will you give me?” Jia Lian laughed. “Whatever you ask for.” Ping’er laughed from beside them. “Madam needn’t ask for a reward. Only yesterday she was saying that she wanted to do something but was short of one or two hundred taels. Why not borrow the money and let Madam keep one or two hundred? Wouldn’t that satisfy both sides?” Xifeng laughed. “Fortunately you reminded him of me. Yes, that will do.” Jia Lian laughed. “You two are really ruthless. Never mind a pledge worth a thousand taels—even if you needed three or five thousand in ready silver, I doubt it would trouble you. It would be one thing if I were borrowing from you. But now I ask you merely to put in a word, and you still demand interest. You really are extraordinary!” At this, Xifeng turned over and sat up. “However many thousands or tens of thousands I may have, I didn’t make them out of you. People inside and outside this household, high and low, already say plenty about me behind my back; all that was missing was you joining in. It’s true that without a traitor in the family, no outsider can get in. Of course the Wang family never had any money; it was all earned by your Jia family. Don’t make me sick. You seem to think your family contains another Shi Chong or Deng Tong. Yet what could be swept from the cracks in the Wang family’s floors would be enough to support you for life. Aren’t you ashamed to say such things? There is proof before your eyes: examine the dowries brought by Madam and me, compare them with yours, and tell me which article was unworthy of your family!” Jia Lian laughed. “I was only joking, and you’ve lost your temper. Why make so much of it? What does one or two hundred taels matter? I haven’t a great deal, but I do have that much. I’ll bring it in first, and you can use it as you please. How about that?” “I’m not waiting for money to be put in my mouth before I die,” Xifeng replied. “What is the hurry?” “Why bother?” said Jia Lian. “There’s no need to get so angry.” Hearing this, Xifeng smiled again. “It isn’t that I’m impatient; it’s the way your words pierce the heart. I was thinking that the day after tomorrow is the anniversary of Second Sister You’s death. We were close once, and though there is little else I can do, I ought at least to visit her grave and burn a sheet of paper for her, for we were sisters after all.

There is proof before your eyes: examine the dowries brought by Madam and me, compare them with yours, and tell me which article was unworthy of your family!”
Jia Lian laughed. “I was only joking, and you’ve lost your temper.
Why make so much of it? What does one or two hundred taels matter? I haven’t a great deal, but I do have that much. I’ll bring it in first, and you can use it as you please. How about that?”
“I’m not waiting for money to be put in my mouth before I die,” Xifeng replied. “What is the hurry?”
“Why bother?” said Jia Lian. “There’s no need to get so angry.”
Hearing this, Xifeng smiled again. “It isn’t that I’m impatient; it’s the way your words pierce the heart.

I was thinking that the day after tomorrow is the anniversary of Second Sister You’s death. We were close once, and though there is little else I can do, I ought at least to visit her grave and burn a sheet of paper for her, for we were sisters after all.

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Laiwang’s wife came in. Xifeng asked her, “Did it work out?” “No, it was no use at all,” replied Laiwang’s wife. I told you it would succeed only if Madam took charge.” Jia Lian asked, “What is this about now?” When he asked, Xifeng explained, “It is nothing important. Laiwang has a son who is seventeen this year and still has no wife. He wanted to marry Caixia from Madam’s apartments, but since we did not know how Madam felt about it, nothing could be settled. The other day Madam observed that Caixia was grown up and, moreover, was often ill and beset by troubles, so she graciously released her and let her parents choose a husband for her as they pleased. That is why Laiwang’s wife came to ask me for help. I thought the two families were reasonably well matched, and that the proposal would naturally be accepted. But now she has returned to say it was no use.” “What great matter is that?” said Jia Lian. “There are plenty of girls better than Caixia.” Laiwang’s wife smiled ingratiatingly. “That is true, sir, but if even her family looks down on us, other people will despise us all the more. It was no easy matter to find a girl we considered suitable, and I thought I need only beg your favor and Madam’s to bring the match about. Madam also said they would surely agree, so I troubled someone to go and sound them out. Who would have thought we would merely invite a rebuff? As for the girl herself, she is quite willing; I have privately sounded her out from time to time, and she has no objection. It is only those two conceited old parents of hers who have set their sights too high.” Her words touched a nerve in both Xifeng and Jia Lian. Seeing Jia Lian present, Xifeng said nothing for the moment and merely watched to see what he would do. Jia Lian had other matters on his mind and paid little attention to such a trifling affair. He would have preferred not to interfere, but she was one of Xifeng’s bondservants who had accompanied her at marriage and had rendered them good service over the years; refusing her outright would have been embarrassing. So he said, “What great matter is this, that you must keep muttering and fussing over it? Set your mind at ease and go. Tomorrow I shall act as matchmaker and send two respectable people with the betrothal gifts to propose the match, saying that it is my decision. If he absolutely refuses, tell him to come and see me.” Laiwang’s wife looked at Xifeng, who twisted her lips in a signal. Understanding her meaning, Laiwang’s wife hurriedly dropped to her knees and kowtowed to Jia Lian in gratitude. Jia Lian hastily said, “You need only kowtow to your young mistress. Though I have said this is how it shall be done, your young mistress must still send someone to summon the girl’s mother and speak kindly to her. That would be better. Although they are bound to consent, we must not handle the affair tyrannically.” Xifeng hurriedly said, “If even you are gracious enough to concern yourself with it, how could I stand idly by? Laiwang’s wife, you heard him. Once this has been arranged, see that you finish the matter promptly for me.”

p.src: Tell your husband that every outstanding debt outside must be collected by the end of this year. I will not stand for so much as a single coin being short. My reputation is bad enough already; if I leave them out another year, people will devour me alive.” Wang’er’s wife laughed. “Madam, you are much too timid. Who would dare gossip about you? To speak fairly, if the loans are called in, it will save us trouble and keep us from offending so many people.” Xifeng gave a cold laugh. “All my devoted efforts have been wasted. What would I truly be waiting for the money for? It is only that our daily expenses are heavy and our income is small. Counting everything in this household—your master’s and my monthly allowances together with those of the four maids—we receive only ten or twenty taels a month, not enough to cover even three or five days’ expenses. If I had not scraped and shifted money from every possible source, we would long ago have ended up in some wretched hovel. Yet now I have earned a reputation as a ruined moneylender. Since that is how it is, I shall call the money in. I know how to spend money as well as anyone. From now on we shall simply sit here spending it, and let it last as long as it lasts. Things cannot go on like this. Before the Old Lady’s birthday, Madam spent two months in a panic without finding a solution. It was I who pointed out that four or five chests of unneeded copper and pewter utensils were lying upstairs at the back. We raised three hundred taels on them, and only then did Madam manage to scrape together a respectable birthday gift and save face. And you all know about me: that gold chiming clock of mine was sold for five hundred and sixty taels. Before half a month had passed, some ten matters large and small had swallowed it all for nothing. Today the outer household ran short as well, and by someone’s bright idea they have begun rummaging through the Old Lady’s things. Give it another year, and they will be rummaging through everyone’s jewelry and clothes. What a fine state of affairs that will be!” Wang’er’s wife laughed. “The jewelry and clothes belonging to any one of the ladies would fetch enough to support her for a lifetime. They simply refuse to part with them.” Xifeng said, “I do not mean to speak like someone who has lost all resourcefulness, but if things continue this way, even I shall be unable to cope. Last night I suddenly had a dream. It sounds absurd when I tell it: a man came looking for me whose face seemed familiar, though I did not know his name. When I asked what he wanted, he said that an Imperial Consort had sent him to demand a hundred bolts of brocade. I asked him which Imperial Consort, and the one he named was not our own lady. I refused to give it to him, so he came forward to seize it. Just as we were struggling over it, I awoke.” Wang’er’s wife laughed. “That comes from Your Ladyship worrying all day and constantly attending to affairs at the Palace.”

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, a servant announced, “The Xia Palace Treasurer has sent a young eunuch with a message.” Jia Lian frowned as soon as he heard this. “What do they want now? They have carried off more than enough this year.” “Hide yourself,” said Xifeng. “Let me see him. If it is a small matter, never mind; if it is serious, I shall know what answer to give him.” Jia Lian accordingly hid in the inner room. Xifeng then ordered the young eunuch to be shown in, invited him to sit and take tea, and asked what had brought him there. The young eunuch said, “Grandfather Xia happened to see a house today and finds himself exactly two hundred taels short. He sent me to ask whether Your Ladyship’s household has one or two hundred taels ready to lend him for the moment. He will send it back in a day or two.” Xifeng smiled. “What need is there to speak of sending it back? We have plenty of silver; let him take what he needs first. Some other day, when we run short, we can borrow it back from him. It amounts to the same thing.” The young eunuch said, “Grandfather Xia also said that the twelve hundred taels from the last two occasions have not yet been sent back. By the end of this year, he will naturally return it all together.” Xifeng laughed. “Your Grandfather Xia is far too punctilious. Is such a trifle worth keeping in mind? Let me say something, and I hope he will not take offense: if every sum he owes us were carefully recorded and repaid, who knows how much he would already have returned? The only difficulty would be if we had none. If there is silver, he is welcome to take it.” She then summoned Wang’er’s wife. “Go out and raise two hundred taels somewhere, no matter where.” Understanding her meaning, Wang’er’s wife smiled. “I came to ask Your Ladyship precisely because I could not raise any elsewhere just now.” Xifeng said, “All you know is to come inside asking for money. When I tell you to settle matters outside, you are incapable of it.” Then she called to Ping’er. “Take those two gold neck rings of mine and pawn them for four hundred taels for the time being.” Ping’er assented and went away. After quite some time, she returned, as expected, carrying a brocade box containing two brocade-wrapped bundles. When they were unwrapped, one proved to be fashioned from gold filigree and clustered pearls, each pearl as large as a lotus seed; the other was adorned with kingfisher feathers and inset with gemstones. Both were quite the equal of objects from the Palace. They were taken away, and before long four hundred taels of silver were duly brought back. Xifeng ordered half to be packed up for the young eunuch and had the other half handed to Wang’er’s wife, instructing her to use it for the Mid-Autumn Festival in the eighth month. The young eunuch then took his leave. Xifeng ordered a servant to carry the silver for him and escort him out through the main gate. Jia Lian emerged and said with a laugh, “When will we ever be rid of this swarm of outside demons?” Xifeng laughed. “We had only just been talking about them when a whole pack arrived.” Jia Lian said, “Yesterday Eunuch Zhou came and demanded a thousand taels the moment he opened his mouth. When I was even slightly slow in responding, he became displeased. At this rate, there will be no end of people for us to offend.

p.src: Jia Lian came out and had just reached the outer study when he suddenly saw Lin Zhixiao approaching. Jia Lian asked what the matter was. Lin Zhixiao said, “I have just heard that Yucun has been demoted. I do not know why, though, and fear the report may not be true.” “True or not,” said Jia Lian, “he is unlikely to keep that office for long. If trouble comes later, he may well implicate us too. We had better keep our distance from him.” “Quite so,” replied Lin Zhixiao, “but it will be difficult to distance ourselves from him at once. The master of the Eastern Mansion is closer to him than ever, and our master is fond of him too. Everyone knows how often they visit one another.” “So long as we do not enter into any schemes with him,” said Jia Lian, “it should not concern us. Go and find out whether it is true and what caused it.” Lin Zhixiao assented, but did not leave. He sat down on a chair below and chatted for a while. When the straitened state of the household came up, he seized the opportunity to say, “There are far too many mouths to feed. We should choose a quiet day to report to the Old Lady and the master and ask their gracious leave to release a few families of old servants who have done their duty but are no longer needed. For one thing, they could each make their own living; for another, the household would save a year's worth of provisions and monthly allowances. Besides, there are too many maids in the inner quarters. As the saying goes, ‘Times are not always the same.’ We cannot follow the old arrangements now, so everyone must endure some inconvenience: those entitled to eight attendants should make do with six, and those entitled to four with two. Counted across all the apartments, that would save a great deal in monthly grain and allowances over a year. Moreover, half the girls in the inner quarters are already too old to remain unmarried; those who should be matched ought to be matched. Once they set up households, would they not produce still more mouths to feed?” “I have been thinking the same,” said Jia Lian. “But the master has only just returned home, and so many important matters have yet to be reported that we cannot discuss this yet. The other day an official matchmaker brought a prospective bridegroom's horoscope card to propose a marriage. Madam said that the master had only just come home and spoke joyfully every day of the family's reunion; if the matter were suddenly raised, it might sadden him again, so she would not allow it to be mentioned for now.” “That is only reasonable,” said Lin Zhixiao. “Madam has considered the matter thoroughly.” “Exactly,” said Jia Lian. “Speaking of this reminds me of something. Wang'er's son wants to marry Caixia, the maid in Madam's apartments. He asked me yesterday. I thought it no great matter and that anyone could go and put in a word. Who is free just now? I shall send someone to speak for me.” Hearing this, Lin Zhixiao could only acknowledge the order. After a long pause, he smiled and said, “In my opinion, Second Master, you had better stay out of this matter altogether. Though Wang'er's younger son is still young, he drinks and gambles outside and stops at nothing. They may both be servants, but marriage is a lifelong affair.

p.src: That evening Xifeng had already sent for Caixia's mother to propose the match. Though Caixia's mother was deeply unwilling, she felt it a great honor that Xifeng should speak to her in person, and, against her true wishes, went away having agreed profusely. Now Xifeng asked Jia Lian whether he had spoken of it. Jia Lian replied, “I meant to, but I learned that the younger son is thoroughly disreputable, so I have not yet done so. If he really is so bad, we should discipline him for a while before giving him a wife. There is no hurry.” Hearing this, Xifeng asked, “Who told you he was disreputable?” “Only someone in the household,” replied Jia Lian. “Who else could it be?” Xifeng laughed. “None of us from the Wang family pleases you people—not even I—much less a servant. I have already spoken to her mother, and she agreed with great delight. Am I to call her back in now and tell her the match is off?” “Since you have already spoken,” said Jia Lian, “there is no need to withdraw the proposal. Tomorrow tell his father to keep him under strict control, and that will do.” We shall leave their conversation here.

We shall leave their conversation here.

Now Wang'er repeatedly came to seek the match. Caixia had long heard that his son was a drunkard and gambler, ugly in appearance, and possessed of no useful skill, so her distress grew still greater. She was afraid that Wang'er would use Xifeng's influence to bring the match about at once and make her wretched for life, and she could not help growing frantic. That evening, therefore, she secretly sent her younger sister Xiaoxia inside the second gate to find Aunt Zhao and learn the truth. She often urged Jia Huan to ask for Caixia, but, for one thing, he was too embarrassed to raise the matter, and, for another, he cared little about it. She was only a maid; if she left, there would naturally be others later. Thus he kept putting it off and meant to let the matter drop.
